In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of neutralizing epitopes of the enzymatic subunit of ricin toxin, RTA, and the use of this information to guide the design of a vaccine against ricin toxin.
the development of a safe and effective ricin toxin vaccine.
the identification and mapping of B-cell epitopes on the enzymatic A subunits (RTAs) of the toxins ricin and abrin, which are among the deadliest poisons known to man.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the epitopes recognized by the 19 toxin-neutralzing mAbs described in this paper are not only non-linear, but also non-continuous.
the epitope mapping data presented here and in previous publications, taken together, provide a comprehensive and detailed map of all known B cell epitopes that are present on RTA.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified 22 toxin-neutralizing mAb epitopes on RTAs surface, of which 3 are linear and 19 are non-linear, and that 6 of these mAbs have been used to generate a panel of recombinant RTA derivatives for use in vaccine design.
we have identified 6 neutralizing and 4 non-neutralizing linear epitopes and 3 non-linear neutralizing epitopes.
the neutralizing B cell repertoire of ricin toxin is very limited and is comprised of a small number of linear epitopes and a few non-linear, discontinuous epitopes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single, highly immunogenic RTA mutant, such as RTA-3C, is likely sufficient to induce neutralizing antibody responses that are protective against ricin intoxication in humans.

it is possible to identify and map neutralizing B cell linear and non-linear epitopes for RTA, and that these epitopes are clustered in a limited number of spatially distinct regions on the surface of the protein.
the development of a safe and effective vaccine for ricin is feasible.
